name: Architext 1.8.0 Magma Code Graph + Slop Ferret viewer
summary: Adds two optional enrichment viewers. Code Graph mode consumes a Magma-produced Go/Rust call graph (contract magma-code-graph/1) as docs/architext/data/code-graph.json and renders it with a WebGL2 GPU viewer that holds 59-60 fps at 17,814 nodes / 50,215 edges where the existing grid/SVG engine could not. Slop Ferret mode consumes a slop-ferret sweep snapshot as docs/architext/data/slop-ferret.json and renders coverage, findings, and work-queue state as a first-class read-only viewer mode, with a CLI command that bundles slop-ferret plan/discharge/findings artifacts into the snapshot. Both files are optional, so repositories without them are unaffected. Data schema 1.6.0.
updateSource: Shipped 2026-08-05: GitHub release v1.8.0 published at 2026-08-05T09:34:48Z from main f3a6a57, with all five platform binaries and SHA256SUMS attached (install.sh and `architext update` both read the checksum manifest). Verified before tagging in a clean detached worktree of the exact commit — not the working directory, which is how the pre-release compile break was found.

required.title: Consume Magma's code-graph artifact under a versioned contract
required.summary: code-graph.schema.json plus contract-version gating, refusal acceptance (computable:false with a reason), and internal referential integrity (calls->functions, module.function_ids->functions, module_calls->modules). Registered as an OPTIONAL file, so a repository without a code graph is unaffected. Five contract defects were caught before shipping by validating real artifacts rather than reading the spec: tree carrying the sha, executed_target_code against additionalProperties:false, a fidelity minLength that rejected a legitimate empty refusal, null signature params/results, and kind:'init' for Rust const/static initialisers.

required.title: WebGL2 code-graph renderer with call-order animation
required.summary: Instanced WebGL2 rendering via web-sys with GLSL as Rust consts -- no JavaScript, no new toolchain. A seeded Barnes-Hut force layout settles in a Web Worker (a second Rust/wasm entry point built by Trunk) and is cached on (sha, tree, tier). Call order is revealed as a BFS wavefront that DRAWS each edge source-to-target rather than lighting hops all at once. Reachability filters cull by default, so the 17k-node tier never opens as a hairball.

required.title: Surface how the map was produced, without leaking raw tokens
required.summary: fidelity gets no standalone display; it MODULATES the explanation of an edge kind already drawn, so the same picture carries its correct warranty (under rta a dynamic edge may not occur at runtime; under semantic it was resolved by type inference). A separate 'How this map was made' affordance carries generator, method in plain words, and the executed_target_code trust boundary -- driven off the field, never off a language rule. Nodes of kind 'init' get weaker-evidence wording because Magma models calls, not uses, so an initialiser can never satisfy reachability through a caller.

required.title: Render a non-repo-relative file path honestly
required.summary: Magma's Go backend emits absolute build-cache paths for some stub functions (201 of 17,814 in a real artifact; 9 visible in the default view because the filter composes with OR). The inspector now treats file as NOT guaranteed repo-relative: an absolute path is shortened and explicitly marked as not a repository file rather than rendered as source the reader could open. The node is never hidden -- it is real data. The upstream emission is Magma's to fix and is logged with them.

required.title: Persisted lifecycle instrumentation for the code-graph surface
required.summary: The surface shipped with eleven alive-guarded early returns that all returned SILENTLY, so a failure was indistinguishable from a dead app. Adds a bounded localStorage ring buffer (console + persisted, retrievable after the fact via architext_diagnostics()) recording mount/cleanup with instance identity, every alive bail, click hit/miss/ignored-with-reason, layout lifecycle with source and elapsed time, and visibility transitions. This is what turned 'clicking does nothing' into a RefCell double-borrow with a line number. Diagnostics use try_borrow throughout: a panic in wasm traps the whole instance, so instrumentation must never be able to take the app down.

required.title: Deselecting or switching tier no longer traps the wasm instance
required.summary: sync_and_upload wrote the selection signal while HOLDING vs.borrow(). A Leptos signal write runs dependent effects synchronously, and the clear-path effect then took vs.borrow_mut() -- 'RefCell already borrowed' -> RuntimeError: unreachable -> the entire wasm instance traps, freezing every signal write app-wide while the DOM stays on screen looking alive. It fired on routine paths: clicking empty space to deselect, and switching tier. Fixed by snapshotting inside the borrow and writing signals after it is released, with a native regression test pinning the pre-fix shape against a 1000-node ViewState.

required.title: Code Graph mode entry mounts once, not five times
required.summary: The recorded trail showed five mount/cleanup cycles per mode entry, each starting its own 400-tick layout over 17,814 nodes and leaking a RAF closure. Root cause: set_mode wrote mode, flow_idx and view_idx as three unbatched signal writes, and canvas_panel's combined watcher fired once per write, remounting the panel each time. Wrapped in leptos::batch; verified at one mount in the trail.

required.title: Await the layout warm instead of racing it, and show the settle gate
required.summary: The app-load worker warm existed to remove the settle cost, but the tier effect terminated the in-flight warm on a cache miss and settled locally instead -- 15,697 ms on the main thread, every time. The component now awaits a warm for the same LayoutKey (still painting the tick-0 seed immediately, so first paint is unchanged) and adopts its result. Separately, clicks during a settle were discarded silently because the hit-test tree still holds pre-settle positions; the guard is correct but was invisible, so the progress panel now states that selection is unavailable while the layout settles, gated behind a 200 ms threshold so fast settles never flash it.

required.title: Size nodes on a log scale so connectivity is readable
required.summary: Radius already keyed off degree, but sqrt is the wrong curve for a heavy-tailed call graph. Measured on the real corpus (median degree 3, max 888), it put 77% of nodes inside a 3-6px band and clamped the 46 busiest to an identical 22px -- saturating at BOTH ends. A log map widens the crowded low-degree band and drops ceiling saturation from 46 nodes to 2. Rank/percentile scores better on raw spread and was deliberately rejected: it makes radius mean 'busier than N% of THIS document', so the same function changes size between repositories.

required.title: Decay call-order animation brightness on the GPU
required.summary: The reveal accumulated as a uniformly-lit mass, so the wavefront was hard to follow. Each element now lights bright as its hop fires and decays toward a legible resting floor -- a comet trail -- with the falloff computed per-vertex in the shader from a per-instance hop age, never on the CPU. Already-revealed elements stay visible, since the accumulated graph is the point. Measured 59 fps during reveal plus decay, identical to the pre-decay baseline. prefers-reduced-motion bypasses decay entirely.

required.title: Consume Slop Ferret sweep output under a versioned contract
required.summary: Adds viewer/schema/slop-ferret.schema.json and registers docs/architext/data/slop-ferret.json as an OPTIONAL manifest logical key 'slopFerret'. The snapshot combines the slop-ferret Record (coverage fractions, provenance, accounting) with the authored findings list so the viewer has one fetch and one schema. Field names mirror the slop-ferret wire format (snake_case) because the producer is a Go tool. Validation enforces required fields, refuses unknown fields, and renders a non-fatal refusal panel in the viewer when the file is malformed, identical to the Code Graph refusal pattern. Post-review hardening (PR #287): the schema's `severity` and `status` were closed enums against a separately-versioned external tool, which is the kind:"init" shape — an unknown value rejects the WHOLE sweep instead of degrading. The tell was already present, since findings carry a `refutation` field while `status` admitted only VERIFIED|SUSPECTED. Both are now unconstrained strings, with the panel degrading explicitly (unknown severity sorts last and gets an `--unknown` CSS modifier rather than an unstyled class built from producer text); verified live against an injected severity "catastrophic" / status "REFUTED", which the previous schema rejected outright. A validation module was also added for the two things the JSON-schema layer cannot express: schema-VERSION gating (the schema accepts any integer >= 1, so a future schema 2 reusing these field names would otherwise be silently misread as schema 1) and count reconciliation (findings_verified/findings_suspected come from the discharge file while findings comes from a separate file, with no producer-side check between them). That module was declared in mod.rs by #285 but never committed, leaving develop unable to compile from a clean checkout until #287.

required.title: CLI command to bundle Slop Ferret artifacts into an Architext snapshot
required.summary: Adds 'architext slop-ferret [path] --plan <plan> --discharge <discharge> --findings <findings>'. The command runs 'ferret enumerate <plan> <discharge> <repo>' as a subprocess, merges the Record fields with the findings array, writes docs/architext/data/slop-ferret.json, and adds or updates the slopFerret entry in manifest.json. Exit codes follow ferret: 3 (items open) still writes the snapshot so the viewer can show incomplete accounting; 4 (refused) does not write. This keeps mutation-token scope unchanged and avoids running an external binary from the axum server.

required.title: Slop Ferret viewer mode and panel
required.summary: Adds Mode::SlopFerret to the viewer with a dedicated ferret-hunt icon and a read-only panel showing the coverage banner (attested repo/plan, denominator, waived, worklist/unmatched sizes), the findings table sorted severity-first, and the work-queue summary (accounting, families not run, checked-clean, near-misses). Judgement -- which findings are verified -- stays in the skill and the agent that ran the sweep; Architext only visualizes the artefact. Malformed data renders an error surface instead of a blank panel.

deferred.title: Richer-UI design track across the nine SVG modes
deferred.summary: Carry the visual quality of the GPU code-graph surface across the existing SVG modes (Flows, Sequence, C4, Deployment, Data/Risks, Repo Tree, Blast Radius, Release Truth, Rules). Approved in principle by the maintainer during 1.8.0.
deferred.deferredReason: SEQUENCING, not descoping. 1.8.0's viewer work was scoped to the code-graph surface because a 17k-node call graph is a genuinely different rendering problem from the routed diagrams -- WebGL was adopted for that surface alone, deliberately. Applying a design language across nine modes needs the design settled first and a fidelity audit across every mode (rule design-language-fidelity-audit); folding that into 1.8.0 would hold a shipped, verified code-graph feature behind unstarted design work. Maintainer's call on 2026-08-01 was to fold it into the next release.

deferred.title: Consume Magma's limitations[] and disclosure fields
deferred.summary: Magma is designing a limitations[] field (scope / attribution / effect / id) plus a sibling disclosure object of per-run counts, retrofitted across Go and Rust. Architext has reviewed the proposed shape and recommended an array, unconstrained scope/effect strings, and a sibling for the counts. It matters beyond disclosure: Magma's Rust backend over-roots derive-heavy crates (measured 87% of nodes rooted, zero dead functions of 156), which collapses our Dead and Test-only badge sets to empty and would read as a clean bill of health rather than an absence of evidence.
deferred.deferredReason: UPSTREAM DEPENDENCY. The field is unfinalised -- Magma explicitly has not built against it and asked for review before freezing the spec. Adding a new property is a two-sided change because our root schema sets additionalProperties:false, so guessing the shape early risks shipping a contract we then have to break. Lands in the release after 1.8.0, once Magma finalises.

deferred.title: Magma emits absolute build-cache paths for some Go stubs
deferred.summary: 201 of 17,814 functions in a real Go artifact carry an absolute Go build-cache path instead of a repo-relative one.
deferred.deferredReason: NOT OURS TO FIX -- the defect is in Magma's Go backend emission and is logged with that project. Architext's consumer-side mitigation (code-graph-file-honesty) shipped in this release, so the reader is never misled in the meantime; closing the underlying issue requires an upstream change.

deferred.title: Slop Ferret viewer filtering, master/detail, and cross-links
deferred.summary: Add severity/status/family filters, master/detail layout for individual findings, near-misses and checked-clean sections, and cross-links from finding file paths to Repo Tree file preview.
deferred.deferredReason: SEQUENCING, not descoping. The initial slice (Approach A) establishes the data contract and mode first; the file format does not change when the UI gets richer. Filtering and detail work is approved for a follow-up slice after 1.8.0.

workstreams.name: Magma contract and validation
workstreams.summary: The data-side half: schema, contract-version gating, refusal acceptance, referential integrity, and doctor/sync auto-registration of the optional code-graph file.

workstreams.name: Code Graph viewer
workstreams.summary: The rendering half: GPU renderer, call-order animation, provenance surface, and the stability work that the persisted instrumentation exposed -- a wasm-trapping double borrow, a five-fold mount storm, and a worker warm that was being terminated by the code meant to use it.

workstreams.name: Slop Ferret viewer integration
workstreams.summary: End-to-end integration: versioned data contract and validation, CLI snapshot command that invokes ferret enumerate, and a read-only viewer mode rendering coverage, findings, and work-queue state. The companion slop-ferret documentation update was merged separately in robot-accomplice/slop-ferret#30.
